A change request is how a company asks to change one detail of an integration it does not own. An appeal is how it asks AEC Integrations to look again when the owner turns a request down. Both need a seat on your vendor account. Both work on the Free plan. So does an owner deciding a request, on any integration.

## Request a change

You can ask to change a detail on any integration where one of your products is at an end and your company is not the owner. One exception: a company whose Sync Service delivers an integration can ask us to record it as that integration's owner, and nothing else ([For connector vendors](/docs/vendors/connector-vendors)). In the vendor portal, open the integration under your product to reach its own page. A field you can ask about shows **Request a change** beside its value, in the Overview or Integration links section. Choosing it opens the request form in **Change requests**, with that field already chosen. To start from a blank field instead, open Change requests and choose **Request a correction**.

The form asks for three things:

- what is wrong,
- what it should say, and
- why.

Choose **Send request**.

The fields you can ask about this way are the integration's name, description, how you get it, connection name, listing page, documentation, pricing, release stage, and owner. You can have one open request per field on each integration. To send a different value, withdraw the open one first.

Integrations delivered through a connector can be asked about too. The ones a connector product delivers to your product are listed in the **Connectors** section of that product's Integrations tab, each one your company does not own with **Request a change**. Those have no type field, so their type cannot be changed this way. The form lists the fields by these names: **Name**, **Connection name**, **Direction**, **Description**, **Listing link**, **Documentation link**, **Pricing**, **Release stage** and **Owner**.

A change request is a request, not a change. While it is open, the public page keeps the value on record and does not show that one exists.

## Who decides

- If the owner has claimed the integration, the owner decides.
- If nobody has claimed it, AEC Integrations decides.
- A request on the owner field always goes to AEC Integrations, even after a claim. An owner never rules on its own ownership.
- A request about an integration's type goes to AEC Integrations when the integration is delivered through a connector, or when the proposed type would make it one.

A request stays with whoever was deciding when you sent it, with a few exceptions. If the integration gets a new owner, its open requests move to AEC Integrations. They also move to us if nobody at the owner can sign in any more. Open requests can also move to us when an accepted change makes an integration delivered through a connector. You can follow yours on the integration's own page, under Change requests, or across every product in **Messages**, under **Change requests** and then **Submitted**. While it is open it shows "With the owner" or "With AEC Integrations".

Updates about requests appear in the portal, so check the integration's page or **Messages**. [Notifications and messages](/docs/vendors/notifications-and-messages) lists every email we send. Four also come by email to every seat on your vendor account, because each carries a deadline:

- a new request on an integration you own, with the date after which the sender may ask us to review it,
- an owner's decline of your request, with the date your time to ask for a review ends,
- a review request on an integration you own, with the date your reply is due, and
- a reminder three days before that date, if you have not replied.

## How a request ends

- **Accepted.** The proposed value replaces the one on record. When AEC Integrations accepts one on an integration nobody has claimed, the change usually arrives with the next catalog update.
- **Declined.** The value on record stays. You see any note the decider added.
- **Withdrawn.** You can withdraw your own open request at any time, from a confirmation step so it is not sent by accident. A request also closes as withdrawn if the integration is retired, and restoring it does not reopen the request. A request about **How you get it** closes as withdrawn if AEC Integrations finds the integration is delivered through a connector, because those integrations do not record how you get them. In both cases you get a notice in Messages saying why.

## On an integration a Sync Service delivers

A Sync Service sells and runs finished integrations between two other companies' products. If your product is at one end of one, you have three more choices. They sit under that integration in the **Connectors** section of your product's Integrations tab.

- **Remove this integration from our product.** You can use it even when the listing is accurate. Nobody checks it before it takes effect. You choose your reason from a fixed list: "We do not support this integration", "We have not authorised it for our product" or "We no longer work with this company". To say the integration does not exist, use **Report that it is not offered** instead. We record the reason and the time. Once you confirm, the integration leaves the public site at once: the pair page, both product pages and the Sync Service's page. The public pages show nothing about the removal. The Sync Service is told at once that your company gave that reason, and how to object. It cannot restore the integration or add it again. It can object to AEC Integrations on three grounds only: the removal came from an account that should not have had access, it named the wrong product, or its reason is plainly false on its face. For example, your own public pages may show that you support the integration. We answer an objection within five business days of receiving it. If we agree, the removal ends and the integration returns. We may also end a removal where your claim to the product ends or is suspended, or where the law requires it. We tell both companies why. Your company can bring it back too: choose **Withdraw the removal** in **Messages**. If the other product's vendor removed it too, it returns only when both have withdrawn.
- **Report that it is not offered.** Use it when the integration does not exist or is no longer sold. AEC Integrations decides. The integration stays listed while we check. If we confirm it, we take it off the site within five business days.
- **Report a wrong data flow.** Choose one data flow, say what is right, and give your reason. Once the Sync Service has claimed the integration, it decides. Before then, AEC Integrations decides. If the Sync Service declines, you can ask AEC Integrations to review it within 30 days, as below. Our view is advice, and the Sync Service decides the listing of that data flow. If a public source shows the flow is wrong, you can still ask for a correction under the [Listing Accuracy Policy](/legal/listing-accuracy). Once the Sync Service has claimed the integration, it maintains the data flows. If a public source we can verify shows one is wrong, we correct it or remove it from the site within five business days. The rest of the integration stays listed. We tell the Sync Service why, and it cannot undo the correction.

You find every removal and report in **Messages**, under **Sync Service integrations on your products**. None of these choices appears on an integration through an integration platform, or one a company builds itself. Use **Request a change** there.

A company with no vendor account can email [support@aecintegrations.com](mailto:support@aecintegrations.com) instead. We check that the sender speaks for the product's company, then take the integration off its product for it.

## When your integration is asked about

Once your company has claimed an integration, requests about its details come to you on that integration's own page, under **Change requests**. You can also see them, across every product, in **Messages** under **Change requests** and then **Received**. Each one shows the value on record, the proposed value, and the reason.

Every seat on your vendor account gets an email when a request arrives. It gives the date 30 days on. If you have not answered by then, the sender may ask AEC Integrations to review it. You can still answer until it does. Until you answer, the daily reminder email counts your open requests, in one line such as "2 change requests are waiting for your answer".

- **Accept** writes the proposed value to the public page straight away.
- **Decline** leaves the value as it is. You can add a note, which the sender sees.

On an integration delivered through a connector, you decide requests on any plan. A request about its type still goes to AEC Integrations.

Editing a field yourself does not close a request on it. The request stays open until you decide it.

Requests sent before you claimed the integration stay with AEC Integrations.

When AEC Integrations accepts a request that changes a value your company holds, you are told in **Messages**, with the field and the reason. The sender gets its own notice. If you disagree, see [If AEC Integrations changes something you hold](/docs/vendors/owning-an-integration#if-aec-integrations-changes-something-you-hold).

## Ask AEC Integrations to review an owner's decision

If an owner declined your request, or left it unanswered, you can ask us to review it. Open it on the integration's page or in **Messages** and choose **Ask AEC Integrations to review**.

The time limits are counted in whole days, and the portal shows each deadline:

- After a decline, you have 30 days to ask.
- If the owner has not answered, you can ask from day 30 after you sent the request until day 60.
- The owner can reply once, within 14 days of your request.

We read both sides and say which one we agree with. Our view is advice. It does not change the integration, because the owner keeps its details, and the value on record stays unless the owner changes it. If our review shows a factual error we can verify against a public source, we may correct it under the [Listing Accuracy Policy](/legal/listing-accuracy). If we agree with the owner, you cannot ask about that field again for 90 days unless its value changes.

You can ask once per request. **Withdraw review request** cancels it, and a withdrawn request cannot be sent again. Only requests an owner decided can be reviewed this way. A request AEC Integrations decided has already had our answer.

Nothing about a request or a review is public. Each side sees the other's reason, note and reply. There is no back-and-forth conversation: see [Current limits](/docs/vendors#current-limits).

## If you are the owner and a review is requested

You see the request in **Messages** under **Change requests**, and on the integration's own page under Change requests. Every seat on your vendor account also gets an email with the date your reply is due, and a reminder three days before it if you have not replied. You can reply once, within 14 days. Our view is advice to you both. We do not change your integration.

## If AEC Integrations hides your listing

AEC Integrations can take your company, or one of your products, off the public site for a while. We do this when we review a complaint, when a court order or lawful process requires it, or when a company is defunct or a product is discontinued. A hide is not a finding that your listing is false. Nothing is deleted, and when we put the listing back it returns exactly as it was.

Hiding your company also hides every product listed under it. That includes a product your company shares with another company. While a listing is hidden:

- its pages answer "not found", and it leaves search, the sitemap, and every count and list on the site;
- integrations with a hidden product leave the other products' pages too;
- your portal keeps working, and your edits still save. They show once the listing is back.

You see a banner at the top of your dashboard, or on the product's own page, that reads "Hidden from the public site by AEC Integrations on (date)". It gives our reason. In **Messages** you get a notice when we hide a listing and another when we put it back, each with our reason. Another company that holds a product we hid gets the same notices for that product.

To dispute a hide, email [support@aecintegrations.com](mailto:support@aecintegrations.com) and quote the message.

## If AEC Integrations hides one detail

Someone can send us a public source that says one detail on your listing is wrong, such as a headquarters city, a link or a description. While we check it, we can hide that one detail. Hiding is an interim step while we verify, not a finding that the value is false.

While a detail is hidden:

- the public page shows the field blank with "Under review. AEC Integrations is checking this detail.";
- the detail leaves search too;
- readers do not see our reason or the source.

In **Messages** you get a notice with our reason. In the portal the field carries a note: "Hidden from your public page while AEC Integrations checks it. Saving a change to this field ends the hide." The note shows our reason and the source we received. You can still edit the field. If you save a change to it, the hide ends and your new value goes public.

We aim to hide the detail within two business days of receiving the source, and to decide within five. When we decide, one of two things happens, and you get a notice either way:

- we put the detail back as it was, because it is right;
- we correct it, and the page's "About this listing" panel shows "Corrected by AEC Integrations on (date)" for that detail.

To dispute a hide, email [support@aecintegrations.com](mailto:support@aecintegrations.com) and quote the message.
